At its core, this is a great game.

I play once in a while with friends (off and on over the past few years), but we don't want to grind the game to get all the content that we technically paid for. It's a shame because this game is a fantastic party game, but you shouldn't have to grind to make the game reach its fullest potential. I'd be fine if the cosmetics were locked behind the in-game coin wall, but not game modes and modifiers.

After a long, hard day, my family and I play this game every single night for half an hour, as a little family bonding time.  We all get to laugh and relax, and it's just a lot of fun.

It's 4-player warioware.  It never really feels like the same game twice.  Everyone has fun, and even when you're eliminated, you're never out of the game long.

If it looks like something you might enjoy, and you're on the fence about it -- if you have people to play with locally, it's extremely enjoyable.  If you're looking for an online-only experience, you might be disappointed.  I've experienced connection issues in well over half of the games I played online over gigabit fiber.

However, as a local experience, there have been few games as fun as this one.  I enjoy it just as much as my 9 year old and my moderately-interested-in-games wife.  I can't give it much higher praise than that.

Time to have a blast with friends or witness those friendships come to an end in the mini-game mayhem that is Move Or Die.

[u]Move >>> The Good:[/u]

From my viewpoint, it seems as though there was more mini-games in Move or Die, but in total, there’s only 27. Now although the quantity seems disappointing, the variety is not. Be it the mini-games or the modifiers that you’ll see as well, there’s always a twist to the games you play.

The mini-games ranges from avoiding a homing rocket or a laser controlled by your opponent, finish first in a race, duel your opponents with rifles or chainsaws, splatter yourself all over the room or clean up most of the mess, steal more treasure than your opponents,… I think you get the idea, there’s lots to choose from.


[u]Or >>> The Bad:[/u]

You can acquire more content through leveling up and the content ranges from more mini-games, different characters to choose from or other miscellaneous stuff. There’s a problem with this though, because of the amount of content that can be unlocked, unlocking everything can take “Hours”.

To save time, you can purchase said content through the marketplace on Steam, but not everyone will want to make those purchases, especially when you can unlock everything in-game in the first place.

Another problem that should be mentioned is that when you get new content from leveling up, sometimes what you get is not new at all, rather something you got already. This can be frustrating for those that seek to unlock everything in the game.


[u]Die >>> The Ugly:[/u]

As mentioned in the previous section, you need to level up in order to unlock new content. The best way to do that is by playing multiplayer games and winning them will be even better. When playing a multiplayer game, should the host quit the game early, the match ends immediately.

This can be frustrating to the others involved, because they don’t get any experience or any sort of compensation for the host quitting the game prematurely, nor is the designated host of the match switched to another player.

Overall, I like this game... but not nearly as much as I had hoped to like it.

Right off the bat, there is too much text on screen -- in too many font sizes ranging from big to tiny -- with poor use of whitespace.  That is a UI fail.  There could be half the text without making the interface any less informative or any more confusing... which it also suffers from.

The game itself, however, is quite a bit better than the UI betrays, but still lacking tweaking for a wider audience.  In my opinion the game runs too fast to be very likable.  I'm primarily a social gamer and a big fan of Worms and games that run at about that speed.  Bomberman and Super Smash Bros are at my upper limit, but beyond the upper limit of some people I play with.  This game feels like it runs about 25% faster than Bomberman.  So, while I expect the majority of the latest generation of fast-twitch gamers like this speed, I suspect it is also excluding many from liking it more -- certainly me and some of my friends.

Too high of speed and a lack of entry-level ramping is a common mistake I see among indie developers.  If the primary play testers are also the developers, it is easy to lose sight of what is the proper amount of ramping for new players.  I suspect the overall clock speed was never fully (or properly) play tested here in search of the sweet spot that appeals the broadest audience while not losing your core audience.  Even if you can't afford a huge test effort there are still ways to work with a small test group (one-on-one and in tiny nibbles is how I do it) to find what you are looking for.  This isn't the forum to get into that, so I'll move on.

A 10% drop in overall clock would probably go a long way in feel of taming the extreme hyperaction of the game.  The devs could, for example, drop the clock a bit, call that "normal", then maybe also create beginner and advanced speeds.  The problem there, however, is it changes the online play settings probably too much, and might also create whiners in couch parties who don't like to play it slow.  Also, a game with too many options generally tells me that the devs don't know how to get it right on their own.  Regardless, I would at least consider such options.

Furthermore, the hyperaction and other speed problems with the game aren't just related to the game loop clock.  I'm the type of gamer that enjoys taking a bit of time after each game (or major game event) to look back and analyze or relive how I got there.  Games that allow me to do that are clearly the one's I enjoy most when I analyze my favorites.  This game is so quick to pull the trigger on the end of one round and move you onto the next that I get no chance to look at why anyone (including me) won or lost.  And, that alone, pretty much makes me wanna throw the game in the bin and go do something more fulfilling... which is too bad considering the potential I see here.

Move or Die is a hectic brawler with tons of minigames, Local and Online multiplayer, Workshop support and a great graphic style. Great with friends and a must have for any fan of local brawlers

You can play the game with up to 4 players, Local, Online but also with bots, You can play Online with a local friend, a random dude from the internet and a bot in the same game for example, So there will always be someone or something to play against,

There is no shortage of minigames here, The amount is just insane, But they all have one thing in common, You have to keep moving or you will explode. It is a nice twist, The minigames will be picked from a random list by the players and then played randomly, Some games can be a bit confusing for first time players, There is a explanation for each minigame, but this gets skipped pretty easily by a button press from any player.

The game also has plenty of narrators, you can pick one that you like, they are pretty funny and really add to the game. There are also mutators, these can be picked by a random player every few rounds, They can really change the rules of the game, like messing with gravity, but some are pretty stupid, like naked players for example.

The Workshop lets you create your own characters, levels, gamemodes, etc. The game has no limits and virtually an endless amount of content. But the content in the main game already feels endless, It really is worth every penny

[h1]Move or die is a very fun game, but fails to execute on aspects of gameplay[/h1]
Move or die is a party game that encourages you to rage, most of the gamemodes involve you having to deal with the other players more than the environment, but this doesnt include all, this game is quite a great idea, and is a very fun quick party game, but I believe the game should still be in early access, and this is for quite a few reasons.

[h1]Gameplay [/h1]
In move or die, you can play matches 5-30 minutes long, with each of these matches you get to choose the game modes that YOU want to play and your oppenents do the same. You then play  your match according to the game randomly picking from your collective choices of gamemodes and you playing them in that exact order.

[b]Expierence Points[/b]
You earn xp for every match you play with people online, you are however, able to play using AI bots to fill in for other players, but if you play the entire game without another person you earn no xp at all.

[b]Steam Items![/b]
Steam items are awarded with every level up of your exp bar and items you earn have different rarities. You earn characters and gamemodes by leveling up, characters are purely cosmetic and provide no in-game benefit, while gamemodes give the player the ability to choose that in thier list of gamemodes to play for any given match! Players can still play gamemodes they dont have, but they have to rely on another player having it and putting it up for individual matches.

[b] Gamemodes [/b]
There is many different gamemodes (I believe a little over 15 or so)  that challenge the player with moving, each gamemode has a different objective and it is up to you to master them and beat everyone who stands in your way. The devs have said they will continue to release new gamemodes and characters as future updates continue, but really as this game is not in early access, there really should be alot more features by now. 

[b] Gamestate [/b]
 Right now the state of the game is okay, connection can get really bad, and it gives the host a slight advantage every match, which is a big deal, but the devs are working on the feature, and hopefully they will put all effort towards it and stop giving us wierd updates like this "mutator update" that gives more of an RNG taste to the game and veers from the skill aspect of the game a bit.

This game is amazing!  For such a simple game, it is a ton of fun!  I just can't get enough of it!  Its also fun for the whole family, since there really isn't anything that inapropreate in Move or Die.   I love most of the mutators, especially the Jet Packs and the Double Jump.  I could really go without the Hardcore and decoy mutators through.

I only have a couple of small criticisms.  The first is that its almost impossible to level up and unlock more content unless you are online.  There is the Daily Challenge, and you can level up that way, but its really hard, since you fail as soon as you die.  I'm rarely able to get past the first randomely selected game mode without dying, especially since the mutator that they choose.  It would have taken me forever to get to where I am now if I had to relay on the daily challenge only to level up.  A story mode would be great, but it doesn't really need one.  Although you could play it by yourself, if you use bots, its really meant as a game to play with other people.

On the bright side, if you really want more content and don't want to have to work for it, there are plenty of mods for this game.  However, I don't think that you can use the user created characters in online matches, only in offline couch matches, from what I understand.  I have never installed any mods for this game, and I'm not sure exactly how they work.  I also generally don't feel comfortable using mods, but if you are not like me in that regard, they're another thing that you could use to keep the game fresh.
Quick matches and plenty of mayhem, it’s easy to learn, and the minigames make everything really fun, on offer the price is very reasonable, so it’s well worth picking up on Steam.

I was leary of the fairly high price tag of this game - but it's totally justified. Around here we play any local couch games we can get our hands on and I can confidently say that [i]Move or Die[/i] is hands-down pure fun. 

With both online play and local madness, it's always easy to get a game going. Overall, [i]Move or Die[/i] is highly polished. There are tons of avatars you can earn as you level up, and lots of built in player interaction. I think this is definately a game that you have to play to truly experience the fun factor. Kind of like [i]TowerFall[/i], in a way.

[b]Pros:[/b]
+Online and local play.
+It can be described as a series of really well done mini-games. You then select how long you want to play, followed by what mini-games you want in the mix. We thought they were all fun.
+Artwork and music are great!
+Easy to pick up and learn. We had a mix of gaming veterans and fairly new people, and it wasn't unbalanced.

The downfall and abandonment of this game should be studied. Xelu and Those Awesome Guys had an extremely fun and good game on their hands and decided to just let it rot while removing basic features of all online games patch after patch.

For context, I've played this game for nearly 1,000 hours, am one of the 5 members of the Rainbow Elite leaderboard, and have seen this game's lifespan from around March 2017 to now, and can say for certainty that this game is a shell of what it once was.

Back when I started playing, the game had far more forms of player communication than what we have now. We used to have a global chat in the menu where everyone could talk to one another, we had in-game chat (which even came with a fun little system where bots could send goofy trash talk messages), and you could spam your emotes as much as you wanted. The game was also frequently getting patches with new content, bug fixes, quality of life changes, etc. Basically you could tell the devs had a passion for the game they had made, and were doing their utmost to provide a fun experience for their players.

For some reason though, around mid-2019, development started slowing down, with the last major update being in June of that year with the addition new game modes like Shuriken Parry, Paper Planes, and Radiation, as well as the What the Golf, Astral Projection, and Accelerate Mutators.

It wouldn't be until March / April 2022 when we'd get any kind of significant content added to the game, as everything between then would just be bug fixes, translation updates, and character skins for the most part. This update would attempt (and fail) to make the Ghostly Jumps Mutator less cancer to deal with, but more importantly came with the addition of the game's final new game mode, Pandora's Blast. This would be the last remotely decent patch the game ever got.

Just around 2 weeks after Pandora's Blast got added, the in-game chat (as well as global chat) were removed for seemingly no reason in a patch that did absolutely nothing except that. This caused a lot of problems, namely making it no longer possible to tell if someone left / got disconnected due to lack of chat messages showing that. It also made the "AI Bot Chat Sentience" and Profanity Filter options in the settings do nothing anymore since there's no chat. Most importantly though, it just removed the feeling of playing with other people, since there was just no communication anymore.

I would be permanently banned from the game's community here on Steam not too long after for quote "Promoting toxicity and using racial slurs in-game", something that's simply not true. What actually happened was that I was voicing my disappointment with the removal of the in-game chat, and saying that the devs behind this game would never survive a L4D2 lobby if they can't handle some simple banter in a casual party game.

From here, updates for the game would slowly fizzle out. We had a crossover with Dead by Daylight that nobody remembers and didn't attract more than a handful of new players, we never got anymore new game modes or Mutators, features like the Daily Contribution and Bid War would be left to rot with nothing new added, emotes would become limited so you couldn't spam them, until the final update just after the 8th Anniversary in 2024. A simple patch that did nothing beyond fixing crashes related to missing DLL files and Chinese fonts.

Why the devs decided to remove basic online gaming features and leave the game to rot is anyone's guess. My assumption would be a lack of consistent players, but removing features, leaving us with awful peer-to-peer lobbies instead of dedicated servers, and adding nothing meaningful for years at a time isn't exactly going to entice people to buy your game. I can't recommend this game to anyone anymore, go buy something else.

Move or Die is a brilliant game! 

So a quick peek at the type of games I own doesn't really lead to titles such as this (though since becoming a little obsessed with MoD I have bought "similar" games in a fancy schmancy bundle of couch co-op titles). I was enticed in by the Rick and Morty cameos and once I'd watched a couple of videos I decided to give it a go. Best. Decision. Ever! 

The game is made up of multiple game modes to play online, via local network or just a load of controllers and a sofa crammed with four people. I personally tend to use a Steam controller or an Xbox 360 controller to play the game and find the controls pretty easy to use. Lag is occasionally a problem but this is always the case with online games, and shouldn't put people off missing out on this gem.

The rounds are basically mini games that you play against three other players (or AI bots) and you earn points based on how well you play. The points from each round are then added to your score, and the first to a predetermined amount (usually 50) wins. I really enjoy that when playing online, each player (not just the host) gets to choose game modes and mutators (minor changes to the game, such as jetpacks and double jump) that are played in each round. This is particularly good when your opponents have unlocked game modes that you haven't, and vice versa. 

I did find that there was a bit of a learning curve with some of the levels. My first few rounds were abysmal! But once I got the hang of what I needed to do, I started to win rounds and eventually win matches overall! I find the daily challenges can sometimes be frustratingly difficult, but the game is so fun it almost doesn't matter. 
The community itself is pretty much always friendly and fun, I've only ever once had a player throw their toys out of the pram, and this was just a case of a sore loser. It was a full on "ur cheating ermagherd?!?11!?!!!eleventyone11!11!!" and rage quit, but the game is wonderfully equipped to deal with people leaving mid game by applying a penalty to repeat offenders and retaining all XP earned whilst the opponent was in play. Thanks, devs!

It has now become an almost nightly ritual in our house to play the daily challenge and a few online matches. There's a fierce rivalry going on and gods forbid if one of us chooses a mutator that the other hates! It has yet to ruin friendships but I can completely see why it might! 

DON'T GET BITTER, JUST GET BETTER!

11/10 Mario Party sucks ass.

I really wanted to like this game. It's got a lot of fun mini-games which are a lot of fun to play with friends, but some terrible design decisions make this game extremely repetitive, grindy, and frustrating, so I just can't recommend it.

The main premise of this game is that you must constantly be moving or your character loses health, although there's a large collection of different mini-games which each have their own separate rules, and modifiers that further alter each of the games. At the start of each round, each player selects some mini-games from a random list of those they have unlocked, and then the mini-games you play are randomly selected from the choices made by all the players. Unfortunately, while the requirement to keep moving works well in some mini-games, it makes a lot of other ones needless frustrating or challenging. It definitely feels like a lot of the games would be much more entertaining if you didn't have to constantly be holding left or right on the joystick. A lot of the mini-games are also extremely luck based, which I wasn't a fan of. I wasn't a huge fan of the modifiers either, as they often make the game way less fun, they often don't really work with some of the mechanics or game-modes, and some of them are just awful to begin with. Thankfully you can disable certain modifiers or game-modes if you don't like them, although that only removes them from your choices, so other players can still select them.

The game also has AI players that you can add, and the toxic dialogue that they use in your game is pretty funny, but they are almost always way too good, often completing mini-games with zero mistakes, making them almost impossible to beat, or are incredibly incompetent, killing their teammates or stopping and dying for no reason. They don't seem to know how to play on a team at all, so don't think about creating teams with AI players, because they don't seem to be designed to distinguish between their teammates and other players, and target everyone equally. I wouldn't recommend using the AI players.

By far the largest flaw of this game though is the fact that game modes and modifiers are locked behind random rewards when you level up or must be purchased with in-game currency. This means that you're essentially locked to a small number of mini-games and modifiers until you either play long enough to earn enough currency to buy them or play long enough to randomly unlock them among the massive number of other items you can unlock when you level up. This is an awful design decision, as it forces you to repeatedly play the same mini-games over and over and over until you eventually get lucky enough to unlock or buy a new mini-game, only to have to play that new mini-game to death to unlock a new one. Based on the response from the developer in discussion posts like [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/323850/discussions/0/2798319091577559776/]this one[/url], this was done as a way to have some "progression", but it just makes the game needlessly grindy and repetitive, and the amount you need to play to unlock some of the more expensive game modes is astronomically high. There isn't a way to buy these game modes either, as the developers proudly claim that there game is "micro-transaction free", while not realizing that forcing their players to play for hundreds of hours to unlock all of the content is not any better. I honestly would prefer to have the opportunity to pay to unlock all the content in this game rather than be forced to grind for it. My friends and I were enjoying this game for a short while, but given the extremely small list of games we unlocked at the start, the frustrating luck that many of the games rely on, and how much you need to play to unlock anything new, we quickly got bored and stopped playing.

It is worth noting that you can play all game modes with friends if you play locally instead of online. If you've got some friends to sit down on a couch with to play together, then this game is probably worth buying. You can't unlock anything (characters, trails, modifiers, or mini-games) while playing locally though.

The game looks decent and it runs alright. We didn't experience any bugs other than some minor desync issues (players not dying when they should or appearing where they weren't).

[b]TL;DR[/b] This would be a decent multiplayer game with a good selection of different mini-games with interesting mechanics and good visuals and stability if it weren't for the somewhat arbitrary requirement to always be moving which doesn't work well for all mini-games, the mini-games that rely far to much on random luck, the terrible modifiers, and the horrible grind to unlock mini-games. It's the grind specifically that really brings this game down, so unless you have friends to play this game with locally (in which case all the mini-games will be unlocked to play by default), I don't recommend this game.
